name: Stephen Harper
summary: Conservative prime minister who led a government of lower taxes, free trade and tougher criminal justice, and who earlier criticised the Canadian welfare state and courts. In office he pursued a market-oriented economy and energy exports, a strong North American alliance, and a few symbolic acts such as the residential schools apology.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: As prime minister he delivered the 2008 apology in the House of Commons for residential schools, calling the assimilation policy wrong.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His government's Budget 2009 deliberately ran a substantial short-term deficit to finance a stimulus plan.

collective-defense.rationale: At the 2018 Copenhagen summit he spoke of NATO as a structure for an alliance of democracies and of American leadership.

democracy-best.rationale: At Copenhagen in 2018 he held that elected populists and nationalists are expressions of democracy, and that one-man rule for life ends in stagnation, tyranny or both.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His government withdrew Canada from the Kyoto Protocol in 2011.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Called Canada an emerging energy superpower and spoke for growing oilsands output (2006 New York speech).

free-trade.rationale: Under his government Canada concluded free trade agreements with 51 countries, up from five when he took office (as reported).

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: His 2014 UN speech described freedom, prosperity and peace as forming a virtuous circle, with trade agreements as part of it.

gradual-change.rationale: Reported as favouring incrementalism and distrusting great blueprints.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In his 2014 Knesset speech he said the Jewish people deserve their own homeland and that Israel's right to exist as a Jewish state is absolute and non-negotiable.

leader-cult.rationale: Reported as saying democratic countries do not have cults of personality.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: His government enacted Bill C-36, which criminalised purchasing sexual services and advertising them.

limit-guns.rationale: His government enacted the Ending the Long-gun Registry Act, ending registration of non-restricted firearms and destroying the records.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: His government enacted the Safe Streets and Communities Act, which added mandatory minimum penalties.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Spoke for free-market fundamentals, tax cuts and balanced budgets in 2006; in 1997 placed the NCC on the libertarian side and attacked the welfare state.

nation-first.rationale: His 2010 UN speech argued for an "enlightened sovereignty" that works with other states.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Called freedom, democracy, human rights and the rule of law the common destiny of humanity (2006) and the values behind Canada's UN policy (2010).

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: His government passed the 2011 back-to-work law ending the Canada Post dispute.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At the UN in 2010 he cited Canada doubling and untying its aid and the maternal and child health initiative.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: As prime minister he voted Yes on the December 2006 motion to restore the traditional definition of marriage; the motion failed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: His government enacted the Anti-terrorism Act, 2015 (C-51), widening information sharing and CSIS powers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In his 2010 UN speech he spoke against protectionism and for open trade.

voter-id.rationale: His government's Fair Elections Act required voters to show identification and ended vouching, as reported on the bill page; not all accepted ID is photographic.

notes: Answers rest on enacted laws and votes where they exist; speeches only where no record exists. 1997 remarks as NCC vice-president predate his time in government and are not used for answers except the market economy.
